items.title: OpenAI’s Performance Strategy for 900M ChatGPT Users
items.description:
How do you maintain system performance when AI agents ship 70% more PRs and your user base scales to 900 million weekly active users?

In this talk, Martin Spier (Head of ChatGPT Performance Team at OpenAI, ex-Netflix) breaks down the compound impact of agentic development on system architecture. As developer workflows shift toward multi-threaded AI execution, traditional performance engineering must evolve. Martin reveals how OpenAI scales non-GPU infrastructure, restructures latency budgets, and deploys autonomous performance agents to fix regressions before production breaks.

⏱️ Video Timestamps (For Navigation)
00:00 - The Dual Acceleration: Rapid Growth & Agentic Coding
02:15 - Scaling ChatGPT to 900M Weekly Active Users
04:30 - The Hidden Engineering Cost of AI-Generated PRs
07:10 - Why Non-GPU Infrastructure (CPU & Memory) Bottlenecks AI
09:50 - Measuring What Perception Matters: Deconstructing Latency
12:40 - Rethinking Performance Engineering: The Always-On Agentic Loop
15:35 - Building Autonomous Safeguards, Benchmarks, and Observability
18:10 - The Future Role of Engineering Leaders in an AI-First Stack

🔗 Transcript available on InfoQ:  https://bit.ly/3U7tHnJ   
  
#SoftwareArchitecture #OpenAI #PerformanceEngineering #AgenticAI #DevOps

items.title: Will AI make junior & senior developers equal?
items.description:
Will AI make junior and senior developers equal? Think again!

Give two engineers the same AI tools and goals. The one with deeper domain expertise will consistently get better results.

Alex Porcelli explains why human expertise remains the key factor in determining the value of AI-generated output.

items.title: Public vs. Private Cloud: The Enterprise Cost Reality 📉
items.description:
At Tesco, 80% of workloads run on private cloud, while 80% of the budget goes to the 20% in public cloud.

Why? An equivalent setup in public cloud can cost 8 to 10x more.

Jayesh Bhayani (Sr Director Technology at Tesco PLC) breaks down the engineering trade-offs behind this hybrid strategy.

🗓️ Save the date: The full presentation drops November 20 on InfoQ!

#CloudComputing #DevOps #PlatformEngineering #InfoQ #QConLondon #SoftwareArchitecture

items.title: How Rust made Python packaging 100x faster
items.description:
👉Join the Rust Live Accelerator waitlist: https://letsgetrusty.com/join/wv-tXiYU0_BHes

Why is uv dramatically faster than traditional Python package managers? This video breaks down three engineering decisions behind uv’s performance: downloading only the metadata it needs, using a shared cache with efficient file linking, and running downloads and decompression concurrently with Rust.

Chapters
0:40 How Python packages and wheels work
1:25 Optimization 1: Download only what you need
2:55 Optimization 2: Never copy the same file twice
3:34 Clone, hard links, copies, and symlinks
5:28 Optimization 3: Parallel downloads and processing
6:15 How uv handles concurrent downloads in Rust
7:05 Why Python concurrency is different
8:24 The three decisions behind uv’s speed

items.title: HackTheBox - Pirate
items.description:
00:00 - Introduction
01:05 - Start of nmap
04:00 - Running a lot of NXC Enumeration (users, computers, groups, delegation)
07:00 - Running Rusthound and looking over Bloodhound data, discovering delegation, pre-2k compatibility group, etc
14:30 - Abusing the Pre-2k Compatibility group to login as MS01 and dump GMSA Passwords
17:00 - WinRM to DC01, pivoting to Web01 via chisel
31:00 - Stealing the NTLM Hash, discovering NTLMv1 and attempting to crack it
34:30 - Using KrbRelayX to add the ippsec DNS record
48:20 - Unable to crack, doing NTLMRelay and coercer to trick the machine account to authenticate from HTTP to DC LDAP and then using set_rbcd to add a privilege that lets us impersonate users on this box
01:00:00 - Running SecretsDump with our impersonated account to dump the SAM, get A.White's password which can reset their ADM account password whom has a path to DA
01:07:00 - Updating the SPN's to point to the DC instead of WEB01 which lets us impersonate users to the domain and getting root
01:12:10 - Unintended: Showing a direct path from Web01 to A.White with RemotePotato0 and NTLMRelay
